## TL;DR

Settings at 390px no longer stacks two navigation layers over the content. The phone tab chooser is now a single horizontally scrollable rail of 44px pills instead of a four-row two-column grid, and the fourteen General section chips hide behind one compact "Sections" disclosure that names the active section and expands into the same chips on demand. The desktop tab strip and chip row are untouched. A new test file covers the collapsed and open states, selection, Escape handling, focus restoration and desktop preservation; light and dark captures at 390px plus a desktop capture were checked during the work.

## Work and rationale

The previous mobile composition task (#1115) moved the seven page tabs into a two-column grid and let the General section chips wrap. Each layer was reasonable alone, but together they took roughly 500px before the selected section's controls at 390×844. The goal was not to remove navigation but to stop two lists competing for the first screen.

The change keeps the existing tab model (`SETTINGS_TABS`) and section model (`GENERAL_SECTIONS`) exactly as they were. On narrow viewports the mobile tab nav becomes one flex row with `overflow-x: auto`, 44px minimum height, pill borders, an accent active state and visible focus. The active tab is scrolled into view with `scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest", inline: "nearest" })` after `nextTick`, so deep links such as `/settings?tab=notifications` open with the selected pill visible rather than off-screen to the right. That watcher is guarded by `isNarrow` so desktop never runs it.

For sections, narrow viewports get one button: a "Sections" kicker, the active section label (or "Browse all" when no `?section=` is set) and a chevron. It carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the same `<nav>` that holds the desktop chips. The nav is rendered once and switched between the desktop flex-wrap row and a two-column phone grid via `v-show` plus a `settings-section-nav--phone` class, so there is no duplicated chip list to drift from `GENERAL_SECTIONS`. Phone chips are 40px tall, left-aligned, wrap long labels inside their half-width cell, and the open panel is bounded to `min(46vh, 360px)` with its own scroll so browsing does not push content hundreds of pixels down. Long labels — "Automation & approval", "Activity animation", "Background service", "Remote validation" — were checked at 390px and 320px, where they wrap without overflowing the page (`scrollWidth` stayed at the viewport width).

Interaction details matter for keyboard and touch users. Choosing a section closes the disclosure first, focuses the trigger with `preventScroll` so focus is never lost inside a hidden panel, and then calls the existing `goToSection`, which either rewrites the URL (the existing `?section=` watcher scrolls to the anchor) or re-scrolls when the section is already active. Escape closes the panel from the trigger or from any chip and returns focus to the trigger. Switching tabs closes the panel so it never hangs over another tab's first screen. The trigger is a native button, the chips are native buttons, and no hover-only affordance was added.

Desktop is deliberately unchanged. `v-if="isNarrow"` gates both the rail and the disclosure; the desktop tab strip keeps its `role="tablist"`, roving tabindex and arrow/Home/End handling, and the chips keep their inline wrap and click behaviour. At 1440×900 the tabs and chip row sit where they did before; the only new desktop selector is `.settings-section-nav--phone`, which only applies when narrow.

The new `settings-mobile-nav-density.test.ts` mounts the real view with the full `getConfigSchema()` and asserts the narrow rail and collapsed disclosure, that the hidden panel still contains all fourteen sections, that selecting Board rewrites the query and closes the panel, that `?section=automation` names itself in the trigger and marks its chip, that Escape from a chip returns focus to the trigger, and that desktop keeps the chip row with no phone-only controls. The existing save-and-errors test passes unchanged because the rail keeps the same `.settings-mobile-nav-btn` markup.

## Approaches tried

I first considered turning the section chips into a custom Radix select. The repository already uses that component for real preferences, but a dropdown whose whole job is in-page navigation reads as a form field here and adds a popup on top of the tab rail. Reusing the existing chip buttons keeps the visual language and URL behaviour.

I also considered an inline horizontally scrolling chip rail under the tab rail. It would have been a one-line change, but fourteen topics in a rail at 390px means most are off-screen with no indication of how many remain, and the horizontal swipe would compete with vertical page scroll. The disclosure is bounded, shows every topic at once when opened, and needs one tap.

For the tab rail, the alternative was a dropdown listing all pages. It would have been vertically smallest, but it hides the current page's neighbours, and the tab strip is the established settings navigation. A scroll rail keeps the same labels, order and semantics while removing three rows of height. The partial next pill at the right edge is the scroll affordance; no gradient mask or scrollbar was added.

A smaller option was to trim the shared page header (title, description, search, reference link). That would have addressed the symptom without fixing the repeated navigation density the task names, so I left the header alone.

## Challenges and blockers

The main visual risk was long labels. Section names are hand-written in `GENERAL_SECTIONS`, and "Automation & approval" is close to the width of a two-column cell at 390px and wraps at 320px. I verified both widths in a headless Chromium render against the built UI with a mocked API and schema: at 390px the panel is 332px tall with 40px chips; at 320px chips grow to 51px for wrapped labels and the document's `scrollWidth` still equals 320. Light and dark were both captured, plus an open-panel dark capture and a notifications-tab capture confirming the rail scrolls the active pill into view on a deep link.

Focus after selection was subtle: a chip click closes the panel containing the focused element, so focus would fall to the body mid-navigation. Focusing the trigger with `preventScroll` first fixes that without disturbing the section scroll that follows.

The managed check's test step was skipped here (`REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1`, the remote validation path), so I also ran `bun run test --changed main`: 17 files and 212 tests passed. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed formatting, lint, build, CSS layering, theme contrast, hard-coded colors, the rendered contrast audit over sixteen theme scopes, bare-require and branch-artifact guards, and UI smoke. No config key, schema row, save path or API changed, so no docs or Settings control were needed.

## Key learnings

Density comes from stacking two complete lists, not from either list being too big. Making one list a disclosure brought the Themes card into the first viewport while keeping every topic one tap away. One nav element with a narrow class plus `v-show` kept the section list single-sourced while CSS owned the presentation. Scrollable rails need the active item brought into view on deep links, or URL-driven selection is clear only after a swipe. And for a mobile-only change, review shots need `viewportWidth`/`viewportHeight`; otherwise the automated capture shows the unchanged desktop composition.
